answers.answer: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering. This covers production databases and read replicas, Amazon S3 object storage used for customer data, staging, and exports, block storage volumes attached to production compute, backups and snapshots, and log storage. Encryption is applied by default at the storage layer, engineers may not create production storage with encryption disabled, and automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources. Keys are managed in AWS KMS, separated by region (eu-west-1 for EU data, us-east-1 for US data), rotated automatically every year, and cannot be exported in plaintext. Company laptops have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

citations.passage: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest must be encrypted using **AES-256** or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering.

Production databases and their read replicas
- Object storage (Amazon S3) used for customer data, staging, and exports
- Block storage volumes attached to production compute
- Backups and snapshots
- Log storage

Encryption at rest is applied by default at the storage layer. Engineers may not create production storage resources with encryption disabled. Automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources.
Encryption keys for data at rest are managed through **AWS Key Management Service (KMS)**.
Keys used for EU customer data are created and stored in eu-west-1, and keys for US customer data in us-east-1.
KMS keys used to encrypt data at rest are rotated automatically every year.
Keys may not be exported from KMS in plaintext.
Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

answers.answer: Yes. Every Tidewell-issued laptop must be enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system and have full-disk encryption enabled before it is issued and at all times afterward. Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically. If a laptop is not fixed within 3 days, it loses access to corporate systems until it is compliant again.

No source mentions a bug bounty or rewards. KB-16 §8 (v1.3) has a disclosure process: reports go to security@tidewelldata.example, acknowledged in 3 business days. That is related, not a bounty. Don't answer "no" without checking.

answers.answer: Our documents do not say whether the full penetration test report is shared, under NDA or otherwise. What is documented is a Penetration Test Summary Letter, available on request. It comes from the independent tester (Brightline Security) and covers the 2026 annual test, including the findings by severity and that no Critical or High findings were open as of May 29, 2026.

citations.passage: | Penetration Test Summary Letter | On request |
Re:** 2026 Annual Penetration Test — Summary of Results
As of the date of this letter, **there are no open Critical or High findings.**

answers.reasoning_note: The Trust Center lists only the summary letter (on request). The SOC 2 full report is NDA-gated, but no source covers the full pentest report. A human needs to decide whether it can be shared under NDA. A 2024 past answer (KB-32) references an older test and was not used.

No passage mentions a SOC or 24/7 staffing. Related: KB-06 §7 says automated detection rules send alerts to the Security team's alert queue; KB-10 §6.2 sets triage targets (SEV1 30 min). Neither states coverage hours.

answers.answer: Our current Information Security Policy (v3.2) does not list a CISO role. The Head of Security owns the security program day to day, including leading incident response and reporting on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly. The Chief Technology Officer is the accountable executive for the program, and a Security & Compliance team implements and monitors controls. Our documents do not name the person in either role or give the size of the security team.

citations.passage: **Head of Security.** Owns the security program day to day. Maintains this policy and its supporting standards, oversees risk assessments, leads security incident response, and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly.
**Chief Technology Officer (CTO).** Accountable executive for the information security program.
**Security & Compliance team.** Implements and monitors security controls, manages the SOC 2 program, responds to customer security questionnaires, and supports audits.

answers.reasoning_note: Partial: KB-02 v3.2 gives the security leadership roles but names no person and no team size, so a human needs to supply those. Superseded KB-03 v2.4 and the 2024 answer library (KB-32 A-012) say the Director of Engineering owns security; both are outdated and should not be reused.
